surprises.head: Jeremy Swayman stood on his head
surprises.body: Swayman allowed 1 goal on 37 shots, worth 4.7 expected goals: 3.6 fewer than expected. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 250 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Utah found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Boston usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Utah’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.6% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.1% against Boston) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Swayman stands on his head against the Mammoth
paras: Frédéric Brunet picked up his first NHL point. Casey Mittelstadt, David Pastrňák and Mason Lohrei scored three goals in less than six minutes midway through the first to put the Bruins up 3-0. Utah pulled Sebastian Cossa after three goals and turned to Karel Vejmelka for the rest of the first. The second was all Bruins: Pastrňák scored his second of the night on the power play, Morgan Geekie scored on the power play, and Matthew Poitras scored to make it 6-0. Jack McBain got the Mammoth on the board midway through the third, far too late to matter. Geekie finished with a goal and two assists, and Pastrňák added two assists for a four-point night.

The score flatters the Bruins: the Mammoth had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Mammoth win about seven in ten. Jeremy Swayman was the difference, stopping 36 of 37.

Special teams did the work: the Bruins scored three power-play goals on four chances and killed all seven Mammoth power plays. Will Borgen took three penalties on his own. The Bruins improved to 3-2-0, climbing to fourth in the Atlantic. The Mammoth dropped to 3-2-0, slipping to third in the Central.
